description.narrative:
The Ministry of Employment, Social Affairs and Family (MESAF) and NAFIS, in collaboration with The Girl Generation-Support to Africa Led Movement to End FGM/C (TGG-ALM) are in the forefront leading the fight against FGM/C in Somaliland. Through this partnership, they seek to strengthen collaboration amongst stakeholders, breaking the silos in tackling FGM/C and amplify the voices of the actors in demanding for the much needed change.
MESAF, in partnership with NAFIS and TGG-ALM, plan to convene stakeholders to deliberateon collaborative efforts in strengthening end FGM/C efforts at interconnected levels within Somaliland. The overall goal of the convention is building united endeavors and guided forces Against the practice of Female Genital Mutilation in Somaliland enabling, effective and relevant public policy for FGM Abandonment. The rationale behind the convention on combating Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) in Somaliland is deeply rooted in the stark realities facing its female population. With aprevalence rate of 98 percent, as revealed by a 2020 survey conducted by the Ministry of Health Development of Somaliland and UNICEF, every girl in Somaliland faces pervasive risk daily. The socio-economic fabric of the region bears the burden of FGM, with significant resources diverted to address itscomplications in healthcare facilities, hindering educational opportunities for girls and fracturing many households. Despite deeply entrenched cultural and religious roots, Somaliland's democratic framework has enabled strides in policy development and advocacy for gender equality and human rights. Initiatives such as the National Gender Policy and Social Protection policy aim to address systemic gender-based inequalities. However, combating FGM presents unique challenges intertwined with cultural and religious beliefs, requiring engagement with traditional and religious leaders to navigate these dynamics. Stakeholders have advocated for zero tolerance for the practice, yet the journey towards effective policy implementation remains arduous, demanding relentless advocacy to transform rhetoric into tangible action.
Thus, the convention will focus on FGM Policy advocacy strategies, FGM Abandonment process knowledge and experience exchanges, and building strong working relationships toward the approval and adaptation process of the FGM Policy to end the practice of Female Genital Mutilation in Somaliland in the near future. Delegates from bordering countries including Kenya, Senegal, Sudan, Djibouti will share end FGM/C strategies. Civil society organization in Somaliland and UN agencies and other stakeholders such as health professionals, religious leaders and activists will be invited to bring insights into the convention.

participating-org.narrative: The Ministry of Employment, Social Affairs and Family (MESAF) is the lead agency mandated to advance gender issues in Somaliland. Somaliland adopted a National Gender Policy in 2011. The National Gender Policy is guided by the principles of the national Constitution, the Reconstruction Development Framework and international conventions and treaties. The overall objective of the National Gender Policy is to facilitate mainstreaming of the needs and concerns of women and men, girls and boys in all areas for sustainable andequitable development and poverty eradication. The National Gender Policy obligates government agencies to fulfill some certain tasks for gender equality in creating inclusive and enabling environment for sustainable development. In the policy framework, women should be empowered economically through different means and approaches by reducing poverty rate of women in Somali-land according to National Development Plan II, therefore, the formulation of these mechanisms should be facilitated for women#s economic empowerment: # Financial institutions for gender equality # Available and affordable grant funds for gender equality # Property rights for gender equality and sustainable development
